protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: CONFIRMED: the v1.19.2 generated tokenizer has variable-length \[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,6} escapes inside repeated STRING and IDENT/FUNCTION expressions, and STRING also lets the negated class consume backslash. Node-1 Ruby replays rejected the adversarial inputs while showing old-versus-atomic timings of 0.036826s versus 0.000003s for 20 overlap units, 0.287620s versus 0.000003s for 8 STRING hex escapes, and 0.276810s versus 0.000010s for 8 FUNCTION hex escapes.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: CONFIRMED: 9246422c850b9e580eead224fd17ed5ff5564878 is the first path-history object for lib/nokogiri/css/tokenizer.rex and directly adds unicode, escape, nmchar/nmstart, repeated string bodies, and the {ident}\( rule. It first writes the hex-length STRING and FUNCTION mechanisms. The later single-parent c06a48ae7d4e01f51e1a7a8924b93f55e3fa253b directly removes backslash from the STRING negated-class exclusion and thereby introduces the separate cross-branch-overlap vector; the primary record explicitly decomposes this later component.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: CONFIRMED: 9246422c850b9e580eead224fd17ed5ff5564878 has the single parent 09f133def133eb8c80dd003bf1c70205836f7237; that parent has no lib/nokogiri/css tokenizer/parser tree and no vulnerable macros. Thus introducer_parent_absent=false correctly means the parent object exists, while the vulnerable implementation is absent from its tree.
